chunks: And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:

Regarding two men who entered into partnership in wealth, then made a profit, and part of the wealth was debt and part was cash. One of them said to his companion: Give me the principal capital, and the profit is yours, and whatever is lost is upon me.
So he عليه السلام said: There is no harm in it if they stipulate it; but if it is a condition that contradicts the Book of Allah, it is to be referred back to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious.

key_terms.دَيْنٌ: debt or receivable owed as part of the assets
key_terms.رِبْحًا: profit gained from the shared wealth
key_terms.كِتَابَ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah as the supreme legal criterion
key_terms.مَالٍ: wealth or capital under joint ownership

ai.seo_question: Are partnership conditions in financial agreements valid if both parties agree to them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a profit-sharing arrangement between two partners in property that includes both receivables and cash assets. It affirms the validity of contractual conditions agreed between the parties, while establishing that any condition contrary to the Book of Allah must be rejected and referred back to divine law.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3848 - Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (as), regarding two men who entered into partnership with wealth, made a profit, and the wealth included both debt and cash.
One of them said to the other, "Give me the principal amount, and the profit will be yours, and any loss will be my responsibility."

Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it if they agree to this condition, but if the condition contradicts the Book of Allah (swt), it must be referred back to the Book of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious."
